mainTopic: How סקילה is carried out: clothing for a man and a woman, a kind death (ואהבת לרעך כמוך), and the stoning platform
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says both a man and a woman are stoned with only a small covering, while the חכמים say a man is stoned without clothing but a woman stays clothed. Both sides learn from the word 'אותו' in the פסוק; they argue only about whether it limits the rule to men. The גמרא asks why, by a סוטה, רבי יהודה seems to worry about improper thoughts and the חכמים do not. רבה and רבא answer for each side: a סוטה may go free and be seen again, and shaming her serves to warn other women, while stoning is already the greatest warning. רב נחמן adds that ואהבת לרעך כמוך requires choosing a kind death even for a condemned person. Both sides accept that rule and differ only on whether shame or pain is worse. A new משנה then describes סקילה: a push from a platform two people tall, then the second witness's stone, then all the people. The גמרא explains the platform's height with the same rule of a kind death. A ברייתא then derives pushing and stoning from the פסוק about הר סיני. It ends by asking how that rule applies to later generations, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: How much of a man and a woman is covered at stoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a man is covered with one piece in front and a woman with two pieces, front and back. The חכמים say a man is stoned without clothing and a woman is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A man is covered with one piece of cloth in front. A woman is covered with two pieces, in front and in back, because that whole area is private. This is רבי יהודה's view. The חכמים say: a man is stoned without clothing, but a woman is not stoned without clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by bringing a ברייתא that adds detail to the משנה about stoning a person without clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats a man and a woman the same: both are stoned almost uncovered, with only a small covering. The חכמים make a difference: the man is uncovered, but the woman stays clothed. The rest of the סוגיא asks where each side gets its view and what reasoning stands behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Here, a piece of cloth used as a covering
Private parts that must be kept covered
Is stoned (receives the death penalty of סקילה)

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָאִישׁ מְכַסִּין אוֹתוֹ פֶּרֶק אֶחָד מִלְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: A man: they cover him with one piece in front of him,
phrases.notes: Literally 'one section.' He means one piece of cloth that covers his private area.

phrases.english: and a woman with two pieces,
both in front of her and behind her,
because all of it is private.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
But the Sages say:
A man is stoned without clothing,
but a woman is not stoned without clothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה with a ברייתא that sets out the disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: man and woman are both stoned with only a minimal covering. חכמים: a man is stoned uncovered and a woman is stoned clothed.

steps.title: What is the source for the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the חכמים get their rule that a man is stoned uncovered and a woman is not. This sets up the search for a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים make a difference between a man and a woman, so the גמרא wants a source for that difference. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis; here, the חכמים of the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the חכמים' view in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for a different rule for men and women at stoning.

steps.title: The source is the word 'him' in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the פסוק 'וְרָגְמוּ אֹתוֹ', 'they shall stone him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And they shall stone him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source is the word 'אותו' ('him') in the פסוק about stoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'him' looks extra, so the גמרא treats it as teaching something. What exactly it teaches is not yet clear. The next step asks that question.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And they shall stone him."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by pointing to a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אותו' in 'וְרָגְמוּ אֹתוֹ' is the source.

steps.title: What exactly does 'him' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'him' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'him' teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'him' actually means here. This is a setup for trying out two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that leaves something out can be read in more than one way. The גמרא first tests one reading and then gives a better one.

phrases.english: What does "him" teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of the word brought in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra word 'אותו' excludes or teaches.

steps.title: It cannot mean women are not stoned at all
steps.stepSummary: Reading 'him and not her' is rejected, because another פסוק clearly speaks of stoning a woman too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means 'him and not her,' that is wrong, because it is written: 'And you shall take out that man or that woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reading, that only men are stoned, and rejects it right away with a פסוק that mentions a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'him' meant women are never stoned, it would go against the פסוק in דברים that clearly says a woman is stoned. So 'him' cannot exclude women from the punishment itself. It must teach some detail about how the stoning is done.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a reading that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say: "him" and not "her,"
but isn't it written:
"And you shall take out that man
or that woman"?
phrases.notes: דברים 17:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one possible answer to the question of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'אותו' excludes women from stoning entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against an explicit פסוק that includes a woman in the punishment of stoning.

steps.title: 'Him' means without his clothing, but a woman with hers
steps.stepSummary: The real meaning: a man is stoned without his clothes, but a woman is stoned with hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'him' mean? Him, without his clothing. That implies her, with her clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of 'him' for the חכמים: the man alone, without his clothes, while a woman keeps her clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Him' is read as 'him by himself,' meaning without his clothing. Because the פסוק says 'him' and not 'her,' the חכמים learn that this rule is only for a man. A woman is still stoned, but clothed.

phrases.english: Rather, what does "him" teach?
Him, without his clothing,
which implies her, with her clothing.

steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים, the word 'אותו' teaches two things: the man is stoned without his clothing, and the woman, who is also stoned, keeps her clothing on.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first reading in step 5, gives the accepted answer to step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אותו' means 'him without his clothing,' which implies a woman is stoned with her clothing.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no difference between man and woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads 'him' as 'without his clothing' but applies it to both men and women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'Him' means without his clothing, and there is no difference between a man and a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה reads the same word. He agrees it means 'without clothing' but does not take from it any difference between men and women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that 'אותו' means 'without clothing.' They argue only about whether the masculine word limits this rule to men. רבי יהודה says it does not, just as with other punishments in the Torah, so a woman is treated like a man.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה wants people stoned with nothing on at all. From the ברייתא in step 1 we know he still requires a small covering over the private area. 'Without his clothing' means without regular clothes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"Him" means without his clothing,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא אִישׁ וְלָא שְׁנָא אִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: and it makes no difference whether it is a man or a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's reading of the same word that the חכמים used in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: 'אותו' teaches stoning without clothing, for both men and women alike.

steps.title: Who worries about improper thoughts? It looks reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: here the חכמים seem worried about improper thoughts and רבי יהודה does not, but elsewhere we heard the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the Rabbis worry about improper thoughts and רבי יהודה does not? But we heard the opposite from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reasoning behind the two views, saying it seems to go against what each one holds elsewhere. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים keep a woman clothed, which seems to show worry that onlookers will have improper thoughts (הרהור). רבי יהודה uncovers her, which seems to show no such worry. The גמרא says another source shows the opposite positions.

phrases.english: Is this to say that the Rabbis are concerned about improper thoughts,
and Rabbi Yehuda is not concerned about improper thoughts?
But we heard the opposite from them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the views given in steps 6 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the חכמים worry about הרהור and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side seems to hold the opposite position in another משנה, so their views here look inconsistent.

steps.title: The proof from the סוטה
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה of סוטה, the חכמים let the כהן uncover her, while רבי יהודה says not to uncover her if she is attractive.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The כהן grabs her clothes. If they tear, they tear, and if the seams come apart, they come apart, until he uncovers her chest and undoes her hair. רבי יהודה says: If her chest was attractive he would not uncover it, and if her hair was attractive he would not undo it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה about the סוטה to show that there רבי יהודה is the one who worries about improper thoughts, not the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סוטה case, the unnamed first opinion (the חכמים) uncovers her without hesitation. רבי יהודה holds back when she is attractive, so that onlookers will not have improper thoughts. This is exactly the reverse of their positions about stoning, and the contradiction is left for the גמרא to resolve next.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman suspected by her husband of adultery

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contradiction the גמרא must now resolve: is the debate really about worry over improper thoughts, or about something else?

phrases.english: as we learned in a mishna:
The kohen grabs hold of her clothing,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in סוטה about a woman suspected of adultery being brought to drink the bitter water.

phrases.english: if they tear, they tear,
and if the seams come apart, they come apart,
until he uncovers her chest,
phrases.notes: Literally 'her heart.' He means the chest area.

phrases.english: and he undoes her hair.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If her chest was attractive,
he would not uncover it,
and if her hair was attractive,
he would not undo it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the claim of step 8 that 'we heard the opposite.'
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה, not the חכמים, is the one concerned about הרהור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוטה (7a) about the כהן uncovering the סוטה.

steps.title: רבה explains why רבי יהודה worries only by a סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers the contradiction in רבי יהודה. A סוטה might be found innocent and leave the court, and the young כהנים could keep being drawn to her. A woman being stoned is about to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There, by the סוטה, the reason is that she might leave the court innocent, and the young כהנים would be drawn to her. Here, she is being killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה resolves the contradiction in רבי יהודה's two rulings. He shows that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a סוטה, the danger lasts, because she may be found innocent and go on living among the young כהנים who saw her. A woman being stoned will be dead in a moment, so no lasting temptation is left. רבי יהודה is consistent: he only worries where the danger continues afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: will be stirred up or provoked (by desire)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
There, this is the reason:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the סוטה case from Step 9.

phrases.english: perhaps she will leave the court innocent
and the young priests will be provoked by her.
Here, she is being killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Steps 8-9 about רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה worries about improper thoughts by a סוטה but not by stoning, so he seems inconsistent.
steps.terutzMaskana: His worry is only about lasting temptation. A stoned woman dies, so nothing lasting remains.

steps.title: But maybe the onlookers will think about other women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה: even if she dies, the sight could stir up the onlookers' desire toward other women.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: they will come to be provoked by other women?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's answer. Seeing her could still awaken desire that they then direct at other women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer assumed the problem ends when she dies. This challenge says the problem is the desire itself, which does not die with her. That would bring back the problem for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
they will come to be provoked by other women?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that a woman being stoned poses no lasting danger
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The aroused desire could carry over to other women even after she dies.

steps.title: The יצר הרע only rules over what the eyes see
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers from a tradition: the יצר הרע only has power over what a person's eyes actually see. Once she is gone, the temptation is gone too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: We have a tradition that the יצר הרע only rules over what a person's eyes see.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge with a known tradition about how temptation works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Desire is tied to the specific thing a person sees. It does not easily jump to other women. Once she is dead and out of sight, the danger ends, so רבה's answer from Step 10 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: we have it as a tradition

phrases.english: Rabba said: We have a tradition:
the evil inclination does not rule
except over what one's eyes see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 and defends Step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Seeing her might stir desire toward other women.
steps.terutzMaskana: Temptation only grips what the eyes see, so once she is gone there is no danger.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה is consistent: he worries by a סוטה because she may live on and be seen again, not by a woman being stoned.

steps.title: רבא: the חכמים also seem to contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out a gap. Why focus only on רבי יהודה's contradiction? The חכמים also flip: they don't worry by a סוטה but do worry by stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה a difficulty, while the חכמים against the חכמים is not a difficulty?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a matching difficulty on the other side. The חכמים seem just as inconsistent as רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a סוטה, the חכמים let the כהן uncover her. By stoning, they cover a woman to avoid improper thoughts. So the same question applies to them. רבא answers it in step 15.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is difficult,
the Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult?
phrases.notes: By a סוטה they don't worry about improper thoughts, but by stoning they do.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the question of Step 8 to the חכמים as well.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים ignore improper thoughts by a סוטה but care about them by stoning, which is the same kind of contradiction.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's contradiction is already solved
steps.stepSummary: רבא changes course and gives his own answer. First, רבי יהודה's contradiction is not a problem, as already answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: רבי יהודה against רבי יהודה is not difficult, as we answered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets up his own full answer. First he confirms that the רבי יהודה side is already settled by רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'as we answered' refers back to Steps 10-12: a סוטה may live on, but a stoned woman dies. This clears the way for רבא to deal with the חכמים next.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Yehuda is not difficult,
as we answered.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבה's answer: the סוטה may go free, but the stoned woman dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבא's resolution of the double contradiction he raised in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Referring back to an earlier answer
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבי יהודה side is settled by רבה's distinction.

steps.title: The חכמים: shaming a סוטה is a warning, but stoning is warning enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the חכמים with a פסוק: other women should learn a lesson from a סוטה, so she is publicly shamed. By stoning, the execution itself is the strongest lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים against the חכמים is also not difficult. The פסוק says, 'All the women will be warned and will not act like your lewdness.' Here, there is no greater warning than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction in the חכמים by showing that the shaming of a סוטה has a purpose that does not apply to stoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a סוטה, uncovering her serves to warn other women, so that purpose outweighs the worry about improper thoughts. By stoning, the execution already gives the strongest warning possible. So there is no reason to uncover her, and the usual worry about improper thoughts applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that public shaming of a סוטה is not a careless ignoring of modesty. It has a specific purpose, to warn other women.

phrases.english: The Rabbis against the Rabbis is also not difficult.
The verse says:
"That all the women may be warned
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 23:48

phrases.english: and not act like your lewdness."

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, אֵין לְךָ יִיסּוּר גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.
phrases.english: Here, you have no warning greater than this.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the stoning itself. Watching it is the strongest lesson there could be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by resolving the חכמים' side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים ignore the worry about improper thoughts by a סוטה but care about it by stoning, with no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Shaming a סוטה is needed as a warning. By stoning, the death is warning enough, so there is no reason to uncover her.

steps.title: Why not do both: shame her and stone her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if warning other women is good, why not uncover her too and get a double warning?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let us do both to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. If extra warning is useful, why not shame her as well as stone her?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the stoning is enough warning. But more warning could still help, so the גמרא asks why not add the shaming on top.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
Let us do both to her?
phrases.notes: Both means shaming her by uncovering her, and stoning her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that stoning alone is enough warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If warning is the goal, adding the shaming would warn even more.

steps.title: ואהבת לרעך כמוך: choose a kind death for him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, answers from the פסוק ואהבת לרעך כמוך: even a person sentenced to death must be given a dignified, kind death, so we do not add shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The פסוק says, 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Choose a good death for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge. The מצוה of loving your fellow Jew still applies to someone being executed, so we may not add needless humiliation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra warning is not worth it, because the Torah demands that a condemned person be given a kind death. Shaming her on top of the stoning would break that rule. So by stoning, the חכמים cover a woman.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים cover a woman being stoned because the stoning is already the greatest warning, and ואהבת לרעך כמוך requires giving even a condemned person a dignified death. A סוטה is different: she is uncovered to warn other women.
steps.whyThisMatters: בררו לו מיתה יפה is a basic rule for how בית דין carries out a death sentence: with as little suffering and shame as possible.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
The verse says: "Love your neighbor as yourself" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: choose for him a good death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אָמַר קְרָא ״וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 16 with רב נחמן's rule. Steps 18-19 then ask whether רבי יהודה accepts this rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that sets a limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Extra shaming would add to the warning, so do both.
steps.terutzMaskana: ואהבת לרעך כמוך forbids needless shame in an execution, so she is not uncovered.

steps.title: Is רב נחמן's rule a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים might be about whether רב נחמן's rule of a kind death is true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב נחמן's rule is actually an argument between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a suggestion: maybe רבי יהודה, who lets even a woman be stoned uncovered, does not accept רב נחמן's rule of a dignified death. This sets up the next step, where the suggestion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, רב נחמן said we must choose a kind death for the condemned person. The חכמים cover a woman to spare her shame, which fits that rule. רבי יהודה uncovers her, so it looks like he might reject רב נחמן's rule completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? The גמרא is offering a suggestion it will check.
תנאים, the sages of the משנה era. Here it means 'an argument between them.'

phrases.english: Shall we say: Rav Nachman's rule is a dispute of Tannaim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks whether רב נחמן's rule from step 17 is accepted by everyone or only by the חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה reject the rule that a condemned person must be given a kind, dignified death?

steps.title: Everyone agrees with רב נחמן; they argue about what counts as kinder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone accepts רב נחמן's rule. They only disagree about whether avoiding shame or avoiding physical pain is the greater kindness.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רב נחמן. Here they argue about this: one Sage holds that a person cares more about avoiding shame than about his body's comfort. The other Sage holds that his body's comfort matters more to him than avoiding shame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the suggestion is wrong. Both sides want a kind death. They just measure kindness differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say shame hurts more, so they keep the woman covered, even though clothing may make her death slower. רבי יהודה says physical pain matters more, so she is uncovered for a quicker death, even though it is more shameful. Both sides are applying רב נחמן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, meaning both sides of the argument agree.
The comfort of his body, meaning less physical pain.

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יהודה and the חכמים accept רב נחמן's rule of a kind death. They only argue whether avoiding shame or avoiding pain is the greater kindness.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה is being harsh. He uncovers her because he thinks a quicker, less painful death is the kinder choice.

phrases.english: No, for everyone
holds like Rav Nachman,
and here they disagree about this:
One Sage holds that a person's shame
phrases.notes: This first Sage is the חכמים, who keep the woman covered.

phrases.english: matters more to him than his body's comfort,
phrases.notes: He means that avoiding shame is more important to a person than avoiding pain.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds that his body's comfort
phrases.notes: This second Sage is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: matters more than his shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 18 by explaining the argument in a different way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי יהודה disagrees with רב נחמן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the argument was about whether to be kind at all. It is really about which kind of suffering is worse, shame or pain.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב נחמן's rule of a kind death is accepted by everyone, even when sages disagree about how to apply it.

steps.title: The משנה: the stoning platform and the first witness's push
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says the בית הסקילה was two people tall. One witness pushes the condemned man so he lands on his back. If he dies from the fall, the מצוה is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The בית הסקילה was two people tall. One of the witnesses pushes him by the hips. If he turned over onto his chest, the witness turns him back onto his hips. If he died from this, the obligation is fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and describes the first stage of סקילה: being pushed off a high platform by one of the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סקילה starts with a fall, not with throwing stones. The witness makes sure the man lands face up. If the fall kills him, nothing more is done.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of stoning, a raised platform.

phrases.english: Mishnah

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי קוֹמוֹת.
phrases.english: The place of stoning was two people's height tall.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מִן הָעֵדִים דּוֹחֲפוֹ עַל מׇתְנָיו.
phrases.english: One of the witnesses pushes him by the hips.
If he turned over onto his chest,
he turns him back onto his hips.
And if he died from this, it is fulfilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי קוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about how סקילה is actually done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סקילה begins by one witness pushing the condemned man off a platform two people tall, so that he lands on his back. If he dies from the fall, the מצוה is done.

steps.title: The משנה continues: the second witness's stone and then all the people
steps.stepSummary: If the fall did not kill him, the second witness drops the stone on his chest. If he still lives, all the people stone him, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, the second witness takes the stone and drops it on his chest. If he died from it, it is fulfilled. If not, all of Israel stone him, as it says: 'The hand of the witnesses shall be on him first to kill him, and the hand of all the people afterward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the next stages of סקילה and gives a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three stages: the fall, the witness's stone, and then the whole people. Each stage only happens if the one before did not kill him. The פסוק teaches that the witnesses act first and the people act after them.

keyTerms.meaning: The witnesses who testified against him.

steps.whatToRemember: סקילה has three stages: the push, the second witness's stone, then all the people. It stops as soon as he dies.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו, הַשֵּׁנִי נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאֶבֶן
phrases.english: And if not, the second witness takes the stone
and puts it on his chest.
phrases.notes: He means dropping the stone down onto him from above.

phrases.english: If he died from it, it is fulfilled,
and if not, his stoning is by all of Israel,
as it says: 'The hand of the witnesses shall be on him first
phrases.notes: דברים 17:7

phrases.english: to kill him, and the hand of all the people afterward.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָאו הַשֵּׁנִי נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאֶבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 20 with the later stages of stoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the fall does not kill him, the second witness drops the stone. If that also does not kill him, all the people stone him, based on דברים 17:7.

steps.title: ברייתא: with his own height, the total is three heights
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: add the man's own height to the platform's two heights, and the total fall is three people tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא taught: and add his own height, so here there are three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that adds a detail to the משנה about the height. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the platform is two people tall. The ברייתא adds that the man is standing on it, so he really falls from three heights. This large number is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here.

phrases.english: Gemara
It was taught: and his own height,
so here there are three.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא וְקוֹמָה שֶׁלּוֹ הֲרֵי כָּאן שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail from a ברייתא about the platform height in the משנה of step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The total height of the fall is three people tall: the platform's two heights plus the man's own height.

steps.title: Why so high, if ten handbreadths can kill?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why such a great height is needed, since the laws of a pit show that a fall of ten טפחים is enough to kill.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really need all this? A contradiction: just as a pit deep enough to kill is ten טפחים, so too anything deep enough to kill is ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by pointing to another source, which says a fall of only ten טפחים can kill a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of damages, a pit ten טפחים deep counts as deep enough to kill. If ten טפחים can kill, why does the בית הסקילה need a fall three people tall? The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction: a source that seems to clash.
A pit dug in a public place, one of the categories of damages.
Handbreadths. Ten טפחים is a little under one meter.

phrases.english: But do we need all this?
And they contrasted it:
Just as a pit that is enough to kill
phrases.notes: This comes from the laws of damage caused by a pit (בבא קמא 50b).

phrases.english: is ten handbreadths,
so too anything enough to kill
is ten handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three-height figure from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the fall in סקילה is three people tall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The laws of a pit show that a fall of ten טפחים is enough to kill. So a fall three people tall seems far more than needed.

steps.title: Love your neighbor: choose a kind death for him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains that the high platform comes from 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך': we choose a good death even for a condemned man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The פסוק says, 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Choose for him a nice death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23: why make the fall so high if ten טפחים can kill? The answer is that a higher fall gives a quicker, less painful death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten טפחים might kill, but it might also leave him suffering. Because of 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך', we pick the height that makes death quick. Even a man the court has sentenced to death is still owed this kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose for him a nice (kind, quick) death

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of 'בְּרוֹר לוֹ מִיתָה יָפָה' guides many details of how בית דין carries out a death sentence.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
The verse says: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: choose for him a nice death.
phrases.notes: "Nice" here means quick and with less suffering. That is why the fall is made so high.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23 about why such a great height is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason from a פסוק: the extra height is not needed to kill him, but to make death quick and kind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ten טפחים can kill, a taller platform seemed pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra height is there so the death is quick, because of 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך'.

steps.title: Then why not make it even higher?
steps.stepSummary: If the goal is a quick death, the platform should be built even taller.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let them make it even higher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If more height means a quicker death, why stop at two people tall?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason 'choose a nice death' seems to have no limit. If height helps, more height should help more. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה picked this exact height.

phrases.english: If so,
let them make it higher still!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 24 by taking it to its logical extreme.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'בְּרוֹר לוֹ מִיתָה יָפָה' from step 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If height brings a quicker death, the rule should call for an even taller platform, not exactly two people tall.

steps.title: A higher fall would disfigure him
steps.stepSummary: The platform is not made higher, because a bigger fall would badly disfigure his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would become disfigured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a limit. Falling from higher up would smash his body, and that is not a 'nice death' either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same kindness that calls for a high fall also sets its upper limit. Too low means suffering, and too high means a disfigured body. Two people tall is the balance between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: He becomes disfigured (his body is ruined)

steps.whatToRemember: The height of the בית הסקילה balances two sides of 'מיתה יפה': high enough for a quick death, but not so high that he is disfigured.

phrases.english: Because he would become disfigured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets a limit on the reason: the same goal of a kind death rules out a disfiguring fall.
steps.terutzMaskana: Too much height disfigures the body, so two people tall is the right height.

steps.title: Pushing counts as stoning: the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'one of the witnesses pushes him,' and a ברייתא learns from 'ירה' that pushing is a valid way of carrying out סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One of the witnesses pushes him.' Our Rabbis taught: From where do we know it is done by pushing? The פסוק says, 'thrown down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives the source for pushing. This opens a list of 'from where' questions about סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about touching הר סיני says the sinner 'shall be stoned or thrown down.' The word 'ירה' (thrown down) shows that pushing him off a height is part of סקילה, not just a way to get ready for it.

phrases.english: One of the witnesses pushes him.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 20.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that it is done by pushing?
The verse says: "thrown down."
phrases.notes: שמות 19:13, about anyone who touched הר סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד מִן הָעֵדִים דּוֹחֲפוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִין שֶׁבִּדְחִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the height question and returns to the next words of the משנה from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pushing from a height is a valid part of סקילה, learned from 'ירה'.

steps.title: Stoning with stones: the source
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'סקול' that the punishment is also carried out with actual stones.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know it is done with stoning? The פסוק says, 'stoned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list. Now it gives the source for using real stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק has two words. 'ירה' taught pushing, and 'סקול' teaches throwing stones.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is done with stoning?
The verse says: "stoned."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list with the second method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing stones is a valid way of carrying out סקילה, learned from 'סקול'.

steps.title: Sometimes both pushing and stoning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the full phrase that both methods may be used on the same person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know it is done with both stoning and pushing? The פסוק says, 'He shall surely be stoned or surely thrown down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the two methods can go together: first pushing, and then stones if he is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק names both methods together, they work as one process. This matches the משנה's order in steps 20 and 21: push first, then the stone, then all the people.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall surely be thrown down

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is done with both stoning and pushing?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״סָקוֹל יִסָּקֵל אוֹ יָרֹה יִיָּרֶה״.
phrases.english: The verse says: "He shall surely be stoned or surely thrown down."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two methods from steps 27 and 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pushing and stoning can both be used on the same condemned man.

steps.title: If the push kills him, the מצוה is done
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'או' (or) that if he dies from the push alone, no stones are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he died from the pushing, the obligation is done? The פסוק says, 'or surely thrown down.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the source for the משנה's rule that a death from the fall is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'או' (or) means you do not always need both methods. If pushing alone kills him, the punishment is complete and nobody throws stones.

keyTerms.meaning: He has fulfilled it (the obligation is done)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he died from the pushing, it is fulfilled?
The verse says: "or surely thrown down."
phrases.notes: The little word "or" is the key. One method alone can be enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to step 29: both methods are not always required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the condemned man dies from the push, סקילה is complete.

steps.title: Does this apply to all generations?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know these rules, said at הר סיני, apply in later generations too.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that this is so for later generations as well?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new question and sets up the next step. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the proofs so far come from the פסוק about touching הר סיני, which was a one-time event. So the ברייתא needs a source showing these rules hold for every בית דין in the future.

keyTerms.meaning: For later generations (always, not just at that moment)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא doubts the rules themselves. It only asks how a פסוק about הר סיני can teach a rule for all time.

phrases.english: From where do we know that it is so even for later generations?
phrases.notes: The פסוק was said only about הר סיני. The answer comes next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the proofs from the הר סיני פסוק reach beyond that event.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the rules of pushing and stoning learned from הר סיני apply to all future generations.
